challenges.finding: Publisher reports persistent insecurity keeping several Ituri control points non-functional and disrupting one of 15 Ituri laboratories (14 active, 93%); too few teams and IPC supplies in some Ituri zones, a strike in one zone and insecurity in two others; low reception capacity at four Ituri treatment sites; too few treatment sites and limited specialty products in Tshopo; work still needed on one Haut-Uele treatment centre and on nutrients for specific diets; one functional testing device and sample storage conditions in Nord-Ubangi; missing IPC-trained staff, emergency kits and waste infrastructure in Sud-Ubangi, with weak community data reporting, unpaid community relays and a provider strike; Nord-Kivu care data completeness of 79% with three zones missing; and 9 Bas-Uele suspects leaving isolation without authorisation before a laboratory result. The security section reports missing isolation equipment and basic material at several Sud-Kivu control points and no formal sanitary barriers at some Haut-Uele control points. IPC counts: Nord-Kivu 12 of 29 rings opened, 16 of 20 health facilities and 13 of 28 households decontaminated; Ituri 35 rings opened, 25 households and 16 health facilities decontaminated; Haut-Uele 4 rings opened (printed with an opening rate of 75%, which no whole number of rings gives for 4), 4 households and 1 facility. No intervention effect is established.

Contact follow-up covers five provinces reporting a cohort. Sud-Ubangi prints ND and the Bas-Uele zero is withheld after the contact cohort moved between province labels in earlier editions. Nord-Ubangi prints the same 71/71 as SR192 and SR193. The lowest printed rate is Nord-Kivu (77.0%). The Ituri rate rises from 75.5% to 92.1% with a larger cohort (13 214 to 16 529), so no same-cohort trend is inferred. No zero follow-up is inferred for any province.

vaccination_by_province.scope_note: Nord-Kivu counts people vaccinated: 5 342 in cumulative, 4 999 of them adults aged 18 and over, in a targeted campaign that includes the BRAVO study. The cumulative is the same as SR193, so it is carried unchanged and no daily value is given; the adult split is new and the SR193 splits by sex and by contact status are not printed. The line cites a recent allocation of 2 000 doses, which matches an SR193 logistics line and is not promoted as a stock. No coverage or denominator is printed. Not comparable with other provinces' rows, which count different populations; there is no national total. The line names a vaccine product, which is not carried.

Tshopo counts people vaccinated (15 228 in cumulative) among high-risk populations and front-line workers. INSP prints a coverage of 101.8% against the plan targets without printing a denominator, and none is carried; a coverage above 100% means more people are counted than the planned group. SR193 printed no Tshopo vaccination line; the last printed Tshopo cumulative was 14 968 in SR190, so no daily count is derived. No dose stock is printed. Not comparable with other provinces' rows, which count different populations; there is no national total. The Tshopo line names no vaccine product.

Haut-Uele counts people vaccinated (4 740) among high-risk populations, out of a pre-registered group of 5 693, across seven zones. INSP prints a coverage of 83%; it matches 4 740 of the 5 693 pre-registered (83.3%), so it is not a population coverage. SR193 printed 4 345 vaccinated of 5 299 pre-registered targets (82%), while SR194 describes the pre-registered group as high-risk populations; the pre-registered count rose and the groups may differ, no daily count is printed, and no daily value or same-group trend is derived. No sex split and no dose stock are printed in this edition. Not comparable with other provinces' rows, which count different populations; there is no national total. The line names a vaccine product, which is not carried.

challenges: Publisher reports persistent insecurity keeping several Ituri control points non-functional and disrupting one of 15 Ituri laboratories (14 active, 93%); too few teams and IPC supplies in some Ituri zones, a strike in one zone and insecurity in two others; low reception capacity at four Ituri treatment sites; too few treatment sites and limited specialty products in Tshopo; work still needed on one Haut-Uele treatment centre and on nutrients for specific diets; one functional testing device and sample storage conditions in Nord-Ubangi; missing IPC-trained staff, emergency kits and waste infrastructure in Sud-Ubangi, with weak community data reporting, unpaid community relays and a provider strike; Nord-Kivu care data completeness of 79% with three zones missing; and 9 Bas-Uele suspects leaving isolation without authorisation before a laboratory result. The security section reports missing isolation equipment and basic material at several Sud-Kivu control points and no formal sanitary barriers at some Haut-Uele control points. IPC counts: Nord-Kivu 12 of 29 rings opened, 16 of 20 health facilities and 13 of 28 households decontaminated; Ituri 35 rings opened, 25 households and 16 health facilities decontaminated; Haut-Uele 4 rings opened (printed with an opening rate of 75%, which no whole number of rings gives for 4), 4 households and 1 facility. No intervention effect is established.

Contact follow-up covers five provinces reporting a cohort. Sud-Ubangi prints ND and the Bas-Uele zero is withheld after the contact cohort moved between province labels in earlier editions. Nord-Ubangi prints the same 71/71 as SR192 and SR193. The lowest printed rate is Nord-Kivu (77.0%). The Ituri rate rises from 75.5% to 92.1% with a larger cohort (13 214 to 16 529), so no same-cohort trend is inferred. No zero follow-up is inferred for any province.
